applied.problem: Several overreaches: 'only resistance limits a DC current' is untrue once it turns; no-load current covers iron loss too; 'Some makers' rests on one maker's catalogue; 'runs away' drops the source's 'can'; 'a few percent' clashes with his sheet's 10-20%; unloaded safety needs full field.

'The load does not change it' contradicts the paragraph's own armature-reaction point, and 'Makers add' overstates NEMA's definition and Baldor's optional stabilising winding, which not every shunt motor has.

The worked example holds the same torque, so 'it gives less torque' contradicts it (it must give less to stay in rating); and unloaded safety needs full field, since a weakened field can overspeed at light load (Baldor, screen 6).
Synchronous speed is 120 f / p, set by the supply frequency and the number of poles, as lesson 1 taught; frequency alone does not set it.

The card drops the contested 10-20% his sheet gives, and states the starting-torque comparison flatly though one source says 'as high'; at the same starting current the series motor's torque is higher, which is what holds.
A plain straight-shunt motor can speed up under load from armature reaction (Baldor, NEMA, and the lesson's own explain), so 'it settles a little slower' needs 'usually'.
